items.title: Spectral measure of a real L2 multiplication operator
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space with $\mu(X)>0$, let $m:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and finite $\mu$-almost everywhere, and on the complex Hilbert space $H=L^{2}(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) let
$$D(M_{m})=\Bigl\{f\in H:\int_{X}|m|^{2}|f|^{2}\,d\mu<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad M_{m}f=mf .$$
Then:

(a) $M_{m}$ is self-adjoint on $D(M_{m})$ ([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]] clause (a)).

(b) The assignment $E(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$ on Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and for a unit vector $\psi\in H$
$$\|E(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}\,d\mu .$$

(c) The operator identity $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)=M_{m}$ holds with domain $D(M_{m})$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); consequently $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $M_{m}$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

(d) $E(B)=0$ if and only if $\mu(m^{-1}(B))=0$, and the spectrum $\sigma(M_{m})$ equals the essential range of $m$:
$$\sigma(M_{m})=\{\,t\in\mathbb R:\mu(m^{-1}(t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon))>0\ \text{for every}\ \varepsilon>0\,\}.$$

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); a $\sigma$-finite measure space $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$; a real measurable finite $\mu$-a.e. multiplier $m$; the operator $M_{m}$ on $H=L^{2}(X,\mu;\mathbb{C})$; Borel sets $B,B_{n}\subseteq\mathbb R$; a unit vector $\psi\in H$.

[F1] **The multiplier is self-adjoint.** $M_{m}f=mf$ on $D(M_{m})=\{f\in H:\int|m|^{2}|f|^{2}d\mu<\infty\}$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]] clause (a), [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).

[F2] **Projection-valued measures.** A PVM is a map into orthogonal projections with $E(\varnothing)=0$, $E(X_{0})=I$ and $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ on its measurable space $X_{0}$, strongly countably additive on disjoint unions; its scalar measures $E_{x}(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle=\|E(B)x\|^{2}$ are finite positive measures ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]).

[F3] **Bounded integrals against a PVM.** For bounded Borel $g$ there is a unique operator $\Phi_{E}(g)$ with $\langle\Phi_{E}(g)x,y\rangle=\int g\,dE_{x,y}$; it satisfies $\langle\Phi_{E}(g)x,x\rangle=\int g\,dE_{x}$, $\|\Phi_{E}(g)\|\le\|g\|_{\infty}$, and it is multiplicative and adjoint preserving ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]).

[F4] **Unbounded integrals.** For Borel $f$ the operator $f(E)$ has domain $D(f(E))=\{x:\int|f|^{2}dE_{x}<\infty\}$ and $f(E)x=\lim_{n}\Phi_{E}(f\mathbf 1_{\{|f|\le n\}})x$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]).

[F5] **Spectral uniqueness.** A self-adjoint operator has a unique regular PVM on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ representing it; conversely, if a regular PVM $E'$ satisfies $\int\lambda\,dE'(\lambda)=T$ with domain $\{x:\int\lambda^{2}dE'_{x}<\infty\}$, then $E'$ is the spectral PVM of the self-adjoint operator $T$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

[F6] **Regularity of finite Borel measures on the line.** Every finite Borel measure on the second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space $\mathbb R$ is regular ([[cor-second-countable-lch-locally-finite-borel-measures-are-regular]], [[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]).

[F7] **Convergence theorems.** If $|f_{n}|\le g$ with $g$ integrable and $f_{n}\to f$ pointwise, then $\int f_{n}\to\int f$ ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

[F8] **Support of the spectral measure.** For a self-adjoint operator with spectral PVM $F$ one has $F(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(T))=0$, and $F(U)\ne0$ for every nonempty relatively open $U\subseteq\sigma(T)$: the support of $F$ is the spectrum ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)).

## Proof

1.1 [The multiplier of an indicator is an orthogonal projection and $E$ is a PVM] For a Borel set $B$ the class $\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}$ is real measurable and bounded, so multiplication by it is a bounded self-adjoint operator on $H$ whose square is multiplication by $\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}^{2}=\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}$: hence $E(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$ is an orthogonal projection. Moreover $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(\mathbb R)=I$ because $m$ is finite $\mu$-a.e., and $E(B)E(C)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(C)}}=E(B\cap C)$ because $m^{-1}(B)\cap m^{-1}(C)=m^{-1}(B\cap C)$ up to a $\mu$-null set. For pairwise disjoint Borel $B_{n}$ with union $B$ the multiplicativity of classes gives $\|E(B)h-\sum_{n\le N}E(B_{n})h\|^{2}=\int|(\mathbf 1_{B}-\sum_{n\le N}\mathbf 1_{B_{n}})\circ m|^{2}|h|^{2}d\mu$ for every $h\in H$, and the integrand is bounded by $|h|^{2}$ and tends to $0$ pointwise, so dominated convergence [F7] makes the truncated sums converge in norm to $E(B)h$; thus $E$ is strongly countably additive and is a PVM. [given, F2, F7, algebra]

2.1 [Regularity] For $x\in H$ the scalar measure of [F2] is $E_{x}(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|x|^{2}d\mu$, a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb R$ of total mass $\|x\|^{2}$; $\mathbb R$ is locally compact, Hausdorff and second countable, so [F6] makes $E_{x}$ regular. As this holds for every $x$, $E$ is a regular PVM. [step 1.1, F2, F6, algebra]

2.2 [The integral of the identity is $M_{m}$] Let $g$ be bounded Borel. For indicators $g=\mathbf 1_{B}$ the pairing identity $\langle\Phi_{E}(g)x,y\rangle=\int g\,dE_{x,y}$ and the scalar measures of [F2] give $\langle\Phi_{E}(\mathbf 1_{B})x,y\rangle=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}x\overline y\,d\mu=\langle M_{\mathbf 1_{B}\circ m}x,y\rangle$, so $\Phi_{E}(\mathbf 1_{B})=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}\circ m}$; by linearity of $\Phi_{E}$ and [F3] the identity passes to simple functions, and uniform approximation with $\|\Phi_{E}(g)\|\le\|g\|_{\infty}$ [F3] gives $\Phi_{E}(g)=M_{g\circ m}$ for every bounded Borel $g$. For the unbounded identity function $f(\lambda)=\lambda$ the scalar measures give $\int\lambda^{2}dE_{x}=\int|m|^{2}|x|^{2}d\mu$, so by [F4] the domain of $f(E)$ is exactly $D(M_{m})$, and for $x\in D(M_{m})$ the truncations satisfy $f\mathbf 1_{\{|f|\le n\}}(E)x=M_{m\mathbf 1_{\{|m|\le n\}}}x$ by the bounded case; these converge to $mx$ in $H$ by dominated convergence [F7] applied to $|m\mathbf 1_{\{|m|\le n\}}-m|^{2}|x|^{2}\le4|m|^{2}|x|^{2}$. Hence $f(E)x=M_{m}x$ on $D(M_{m})$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F7, algebra]

3.1 [The spectral PVM and the scalar law] By step 2.2 the regular PVM $E$ of step 1.1 satisfies $\int\lambda\,dE(\lambda)=M_{m}$ with the displayed domain, and $M_{m}$ is self-adjoint by [F1]; the converse uniqueness clause of [F5] therefore identifies $E$ as the spectral projection-valued measure of $M_{m}$. For a unit vector $\psi$ the scalar law is $\|E(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}d\mu$ by step 2.1. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, F1, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Vanishing sets and the spectrum] If $E(B)=0$ then $0=\|E(B)h\|^{2}=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|h|^{2}d\mu$ for every $h\in H$; were $\mu(m^{-1}(B))>0$, $\sigma$-finiteness would give a subset $A\subseteq m^{-1}(B)$ of positive finite measure, and $h=\mathbf 1_{A}$ would give $\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|h|^{2}d\mu=\mu(A)>0$, a contradiction; hence $\mu(m^{-1}(B))=0$. Conversely, if $\mu(m^{-1}(B))=0$ then the multiplier $\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}$ vanishes as an $L^{2}$ class and $E(B)=0$. By step 3.1, $E$ is the spectral PVM of $M_{m}$, so [F8] identifies its support with $\sigma(M_{m})$; by the vanishing criterion just proved the support is the set of $t$ with $\mu(m^{-1}(t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon))>0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, namely the essential range of $m$. This proves (d) and completes the argument. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, F8, algebra] ∎

references.title: D. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem, Examples 7.5, 7.7 and 7.25, printed pp. 29-34 (multiplication operators, their spectral measure and spectrum)
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.2, printed pages 58-69 (multiplication operators and their domains)

items.title: Atoms of the spectral measure and eigenvalues of a self-adjoint operator
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $E_{A,x}(B):=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ be its scalar measures ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ say that $\lambda$ is an **eigenvalue** of $A$ when $Ax=\lambda x$ for some nonzero $x\in D(A)$, the domain-restricted reading of [[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]. Then:

(a) The orthogonal projection $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection of $H$ onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)=\{x\in D(A):Ax=\lambda x\}$; in particular $E_A(\{\lambda\})\ne0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$.

(b) For every density operator $\rho$ on $H$, that is every self-adjoint positive trace-class $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)), the number $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(\{\lambda\}))$ is the weight that the scalar law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ assigns to the singleton $\{\lambda\}$: it vanishes for every $\rho$ whenever $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$, and it equals $1$ for the pure state $T_{u,u}$ of every unit eigenvector $u\in\ker(A-\lambda)$.

(c) If $A$ has no eigenvalues at all, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every density operator $\rho$ and every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$: the scalar law of every state carries no point mass, while its values on general Borel sets remain $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$.

Clauses (a)-(c) are mathematical statements about $A$, $E_A$ and the density operators; no physical interpretation of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is asserted here.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]); a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; a self-adjoint operator $A$ on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and scalar measures $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$; and a real number $\lambda$.

[F1] **Spectral representation.** $E_A$ is the unique regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ with $D(A)=\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}(\lambda)<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A}(\lambda)x$ for every $x\in D(A)$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],).

[F2] **Functional calculus.** For every Borel function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ the operator $f(A)=f(E_A)$ has domain $D(f(A))=\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}|f|^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$, is closed and densely defined, satisfies $\|f(A)x\|^{2}=\int_{\mathbb R}|f|^{2}\,dE_{A,x}$ and $f(A)^{*}=\overline f(A)$, and is the norm limit of its bounded truncations $f\,\mathbf 1_{\{|f|\le n\}}(A)$ on that domain; on $D(A)$ the functions $f(\lambda)=\lambda$ and $f(\lambda)=\lambda-\mu$ give $A$ and $A-\mu I$ ([[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]],).

[F3] **Projection-valued measure.** $E_A$ takes values in the orthogonal projections, with $E_A(\varnothing)=0$, $E_A(\mathbb R)=I$ and $E_A(B\cap C)=E_A(B)E_A(C)$ for Borel $B,C$; for pairwise disjoint Borel sets $B_n$ with union $B$ one has $\sum_nE_A(B_n)x=E_A(B)x$ in norm for every $x\in H$; and $B\subseteq C$ implies $E_A(B)=E_A(B)E_A(C)=E_A(C)E_A(B)$ and $E_A(C)-E_A(B)=E_A(C\setminus B)$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]).

[F4] **Density operators and their scalar law.** A density operator $\rho$ admits an expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ with $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$ and $(u_n)$ a finite or countable orthonormal family; for every PVM $E$ on a measurable space the assignment $B\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a probability measure with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^{2}$, and for a unit vector $u$ one has $\mu_{T_{u,u}}(B)=\|E(B)u\|^{2}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F5] **Orthogonal projections.** An orthogonal projection $P$ satisfies $P^{2}=P=P^{*}$ and $\|Px\|^{2}=\langle Px,x\rangle\le\|x\|^{2}$ for every $x\in H$, and has zero range exactly when $P=0$; moreover $\|x-Px\|^{2}=\|x\|^{2}-\|Px\|^{2}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]).

## Proof

1.1 [$E_A(\{\lambda\})H$ lies in the eigenspace] Let $x\in H$ satisfy $E_A(\{\lambda\})x=x$. For every Borel set $B$ the projection identity gives $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)E_A(\{\lambda\})x,x\rangle=\langle E_A(B\cap\{\lambda\})x,x\rangle$, so the finite measure $E_{A,x}$ is concentrated on $\{\lambda\}$ with total mass $\|x\|^{2}$; hence $\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}=\lambda^{2}\|x\|^{2}<\infty$ and $x\in D(A)$ by [F1]. By [F2] applied to $f(\mu)=\mu-\lambda$ one has $\|(A-\lambda)x\|^{2}=\int(\mu-\lambda)^{2}\,dE_{A,x}(\mu)$, and the integrand vanishes $E_{A,x}$-almost everywhere because $E_{A,x}$ is concentrated on $\{\lambda\}$; hence $Ax=\lambda x$. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 [Every eigenvector is fixed by $E_A(\{\lambda\})$] Conversely let $x\in D(A)$ satisfy $Ax=\lambda x$. By [F2] with $f(\mu)=\mu-\lambda$, $0=\|(A-\lambda)x\|^{2}=\int(\mu-\lambda)^{2}\,dE_{A,x}(\mu)$. For $n\ge1$ put $C_n:=\{\mu\in\mathbb R:|\mu-\lambda|\ge1/n\}$; on $C_n$ the integrand is at least $1/n^{2}$, so $E_{A,x}(C_n)\le n^{2}\int(\mu-\lambda)^{2}\,dE_{A,x}=0$, and countable additivity [F3] applied to the disjoint union $\mathbb R\setminus\{\lambda\}=\bigcup_nC_n$ gives $E_{A,x}(\mathbb R\setminus\{\lambda\})=0$. Hence $E_{A,x}(\{\lambda\})=E_{A,x}(\mathbb R)=\|x\|^{2}$, and since $(I-E_A(\{\lambda\}))$ is an orthogonal projection, [F5] gives $\|x-E_A(\{\lambda\})x\|^{2}=\|x\|^{2}-\|E_A(\{\lambda\})x\|^{2}=\|x\|^{2}-E_{A,x}(\{\lambda\})=0$, so $x=E_A(\{\lambda\})x$. [given, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (a)] Steps 1.1 and 1.2 show that the range of the orthogonal projection $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is exactly $\ker(A-\lambda)$. A nonzero eigenspace contains a nonzero vector, and a projection with nonzero range is nonzero by [F5]; conversely $E_A(\{\lambda\})\ne0$ supplies a nonzero element of its range, which is an eigenvector by step 1.1. Hence $E_A(\{\lambda\})\ne0$ exactly when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F5]

3.1 [Clause (b)] Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be the expansion of [F4]. Then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(\{\lambda\}))=\sum_nw_n\|E_A(\{\lambda\})u_n\|^{2}\ge0$ by [F4], and the sum is zero if and only if $\|E_A(\{\lambda\})u_n\|=0$ for every $n$ of positive weight. If $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue then $E_A(\{\lambda\})=0$ by step 2.1, so every term vanishes and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$. If $u$ is a unit eigenvector at $\lambda$, then $u=E_A(\{\lambda\})u$ by step 1.2 and [F4] gives $\mu^{A}_{T_{u,u}}(\{\lambda\})=\|E_A(\{\lambda\})u\|^{2}=\|u\|^{2}=1$. [given, step 1.2, step 2.1, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Clause (c)] If $A$ has no eigenvalues then $E_A(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every $\lambda$ by step 2.1, so $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,0)=0$ for every density operator and every $\lambda$: the scalar law assigns no mass to any singleton. The values of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ on general Borel sets are unchanged and remain those of [F4]. [step 2.1, F4, algebra] ∎

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 3.1, printed pages 88-95 (spectral projections, point spectrum and the scalar spectral measure)
D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 3.2.1, printed pages 67-70 (eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of observables; a continuous spectrum has no normalizable eigenfunction)

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 3 'Linear Algebra: Vector Spaces and Operators', Sections 5-7, printed pages 18-28 (orthogonal projectors, adjoints and Hermitian operators)

items.title: Support of the spectral measure, the spectrum and the values of the scalar law
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ and spectrum $\sigma(A)$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]). Then:

(a) $E_A(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(A))=0$, equivalently $E_A(B)=E_A(B\cap\sigma(A))$ for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$; and $E_A(U)\ne0$ for every nonempty relatively open subset $U\subseteq\sigma(A)$. Thus the support of $E_A$ is exactly $\sigma(A)$.

(b) For every density operator $\rho$ on $H$, the scalar law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b) satisfies
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))\qquad\text{and}\qquad \mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$$
for every Borel set $B$: no mass lies outside the spectrum.

(c) More generally, if $C\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a Borel set with $E_A(C)=0$, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(C)=0$ for every density operator $\rho$, and if $E_A(C)=E_A(\mathbb R)$ then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(C)=1$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]); a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; a self-adjoint operator $A$ with spectral PVM $E_A$ and spectrum $\sigma(A)$; density operators $\rho$ on $H$.

[F1] **Spectrum from the calculus.** The spectrum of $f(A)$ is the essential range $\{z\in\mathbb C:E_A(f^{-1}(B_\varepsilon(z)))\ne0\ \text{for every}\ \varepsilon>0\}$ of the Borel function $f$ with respect to $E_A$, and for $f(\lambda)=\lambda$ the operator $f(A)$ is $A$ with domain $D(A)$; consequently, for real $z$, $z\in\sigma(A)$ if and only if $E_A((z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon))\ne0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ ([[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]], [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

[F2] **Projection-valued measure.** $E_A$ takes values in orthogonal projections, $E_A(\varnothing)=0$, $E_A(\mathbb R)=I$, $E_A(B\cap C)=E_A(B)E_A(C)$, and for pairwise disjoint Borel $B_n$ with union $B$ the series $\sum_nE_A(B_n)x$ converges in norm to $E_A(B)x$ for every $x$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]).

[F3] **Monotonicity and vanishing.** If $B\subseteq C$ then $E_A(B)=E_A(B)E_A(C)=E_A(C)E_A(B)$ and $E_A(C)-E_A(B)=E_A(C\setminus B)$ is an orthogonal projection with range orthogonal to the range of $E_A(B)$; hence $\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle\le\langle E_A(C)x,x\rangle$ for every $x$. Consequently, if $E_A(C)=0$ then $E_A(B)=0$ for every Borel $B\subseteq C$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]).

[F4] **Scalar law.** For a density operator $\rho$ and a PVM $E$ the assignment $B\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a probability measure with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^{2}$ in every expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal; in particular $E(B)=0$ implies $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))=0$ and $E(B)=I$ implies $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F5] **Countable dense subset.** The set $\mathbb Q$ is countable and dense in $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-rationals-countable]], [[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]).

## Proof

1.1 [The spectrum is the essential range of the identity] By [F1] applied to $f(\lambda)=\lambda$, $\sigma(A)$ is the essential range of the identity with respect to $E_A$. For real $z$ this says: $z\in\sigma(A)$ if and only if $E_A((z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon))\ne0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$; and for non-real $z$, taking $0<\varepsilon<|\operatorname{Im}z|$ gives $(z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon)\cap\mathbb R=\varnothing$, so $E_A((z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon))=E_A(\varnothing)=0$ by [F2] and no non-real point lies in the essential range. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [The open null set equals the complement of the spectrum] Let $\mathcal I$ be the set of pairs of rationals $p<q$, countable by [F5], and put $V:=\bigcup\{(p,q):(p,q)\in\mathcal I,\ E_A((p,q))=0\}$, a countable union of Borel sets. To see $V\subseteq\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(A)$, suppose $z\in V\cap\sigma(A)$; then $z\in(p,q)$ with $E_A((p,q))=0$ for some rationals $p<q$, and choosing $\varepsilon>0$ with $(z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon)\subseteq(p,q)$ gives $E_A((z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon))=0$ by [F3], contradicting $z\in\sigma(A)$ by step 1.1. Conversely, if $z\notin\sigma(A)$, step 1.1 supplies $\varepsilon>0$ with $E_A((z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon))=0$, and by density of the rationals [F5] there are rationals $p<z<q$ with $[p,q]\subseteq(z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon)$; then $E_A((p,q))=0$ by [F3], so $z\in V$. Hence $V=\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(A)$. [given, step 1.1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

3.1 [The complement of the spectrum is null] The representation of step 2.1 writes $V=\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(A)$ as a countable union of Borel sets with $E_A=0$, so $E_A(V)=0$ by countable additivity [F2]; thus $E_A(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(A))=0$, which by additivity [F2] is equivalent to $E_A(B)=E_A(B\cap\sigma(A))+E_A(B\setminus\sigma(A))=E_A(B\cap\sigma(A))$ for every Borel $B$. [given, step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 [Nonempty relatively open subsets of the spectrum are not null] Let $U\subseteq\sigma(A)$ be nonempty and relatively open, so $U=\sigma(A)\cap W$ for some open $W\subseteq\mathbb R$. Choose $z\in U$ and $\varepsilon>0$ with $(z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon)\subseteq W$. By step 1.1, $E_A((z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon))\ne0$ because $z\in\sigma(A)$; by step 3.1 applied to the Borel set $(z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon)$, $E_A((z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon))=E_A((z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon)\cap\sigma(A))$, and $(z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon)\cap\sigma(A)\subseteq U$ by the choice of $\varepsilon$. Were $E_A(U)=0$, monotonicity [F3] would give $E_A((z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon)\cap\sigma(A))=0$, a contradiction; hence $E_A(U)\ne0$. This proves clause (a) together with step 3.1. [step 1.1, step 3.1, F2, F3, algebra]

4.2 [Clause (b)] By step 3.1 and additivity of $E_A$, $E_A(B)=E_A(B\cap\sigma(A))$ for every Borel $B$; applying the scalar law [F4] to both sides gives $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B\cap\sigma(A)))=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$, and with $B=\mathbb R$ this reads $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(\mathbb R))=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ by [F4]. [step 3.1, F4, algebra]

5.1 [Clause (c)] If $E_A(C)=0$ then $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(C))=0$ by [F4] for every density operator; if $E_A(C)=I$ then $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(C))=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ by [F4]. Both statements are instances of the scalar law, and clause (b) is the case $C=B\setminus\sigma(A)$ and $C=\sigma(A)$ respectively. [given, F4, algebra] ∎

items.title: Affinity and trace-norm continuity of the scalar spectral law
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). For a self-adjoint trace-class operator $T$ on $H$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]) and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ put
$$\Phi_T(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(TE_A(B)\bigr)\in\mathbb C .$$
Then:

(a) $|\Phi_T(B)|\le\|T\|_1$ for every Borel set $B$; the map $T\mapsto\Phi_T(B)$ is real-linear on the self-adjoint trace-class operators; and for every density operator $\rho$ one has $0\le\Phi_\rho(B)\le1$, so that $\mu^{A}_\rho:=\Phi_\rho$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets with $\mu^{A}_\rho(\mathbb R)=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b)).

(b) If $\rho=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ is a statistical mixture of density operators $\rho_n$ with weights $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, the trace-norm convergent sum of [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-density-set-convex-and-complete]], then for every Borel set $B$
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\sum_nw_n\,\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}(B),$$
the series converging absolutely.

(c) For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ one has
$$\sup\{\,|\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)-\mu^{A}_{\sigma}(B)|:\ B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}\,\}\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_1,$$
and if density operators $\rho_k$ converge to $\rho$ in trace norm, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho_k}(B)\to\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ uniformly over all Borel sets $B$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; a self-adjoint operator $A$ with spectral PVM $E_A$; self-adjoint trace-class operators $T$ and density operators $\rho,\rho_n,\sigma$ on $H$; Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Projections and the trace ideal.** Every $E_A(B)$ is an orthogonal projection, hence $\|E_A(B)\|\le1$; for trace-class $T$ and bounded $S$ the product $TS$ is trace class with $\|TS\|_1\le\|T\|_1\|S\|$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clause 2).

[F2] **Trace linearity and bound.** The trace is linear on the trace-class operators and $|\operatorname{tr}S|\le\|S\|_1$ for every trace-class $S$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]] clauses 1 and 4).

[F3] **Scalar law.** For a density operator $\rho$ with spectral expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal, and every PVM $E$, the assignment $B\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a probability measure and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F4] **Convex combinations of states.** If $\rho_n$ are density operators and $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$ over a finite or countable index set, then $\rho:=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ converges in trace norm to a density operator ([[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-density-set-convex-and-complete]]).

## Proof

1.1 [Contraction and trace bound] By [F1] the operator $TE_A(B)$ is trace class with $\|TE_A(B)\|_1\le\|T\|_1\|E_A(B)\|\le\|T\|_1$, since $E_A(B)$ is an orthogonal projection of norm at most one; [F2] gives $|\Phi_T(B)|=|\operatorname{tr}(TE_A(B))|\le\|TE_A(B)\|_1\le\|T\|_1$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Real-linearity and positivity on states] For self-adjoint trace-class $S,T$ and real $a,b$ the operator $aS+bT$ is self-adjoint and trace class, and [F2] gives $\Phi_{aS+bT}(B)=\operatorname{tr}((aS+bT)E_A(B))=a\operatorname{tr}(SE_A(B))+b\operatorname{tr}(TE_A(B))=a\Phi_S(B)+b\Phi_T(B)$; this proves real-linearity. If $\rho$ is a density operator with expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, then [F3] gives $\Phi_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E_A(B)u_n\|^2\ge0$ and $\Phi_\rho(B)\le\sum_nw_n\|u_n\|^2=1$; together with [F3] this makes $\mu^{A}_\rho=\Phi_\rho$ a probability measure. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Affinity under mixtures] Let $\rho_n$ be density operators and $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, with trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$, a density operator by [F4]. Writing $S_N:=\sum_{n\le N}w_n\rho_n$, [F1] gives $\|S_NE_A(B)-\rho E_A(B)\|_1\le\|S_N-\rho\|_1\|E_A(B)\|\le\|S_N-\rho\|_1\to0$; by [F2] and continuity of the scalar limit, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\lim_N\operatorname{tr}(S_NE_A(B))=\lim_N\sum_{n\le N}w_n\operatorname{tr}(\rho_nE_A(B))=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}(B)$, the series converging absolutely because the finite partial sums of the nonnegative terms are bounded by the limit $\mu^{A}_\rho(B)\le1$. [given, step 1.2, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.2 [Uniform trace-norm continuity] For Borel $B$, $\rho-\sigma$ is self-adjoint and trace class, so step 1.1 gives $|\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)-\mu^{A}_{\sigma}(B)|=|\Phi_{\rho-\sigma}(B)|\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$; taking the supremum over Borel sets yields the displayed bound, and the convergence assertion follows by applying it to $\rho_k-\rho$. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Conclusion] Step 1.2 proves the bound, real-linearity, positivity and probability-measure clauses of (a); step 2.1 proves the mixture identity (b); step 2.2 proves the uniform bound and continuity (c). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.3, printed pages 121-126 (the trace rule for mixtures of states)

items.title: Mean, second moment and variance of the scalar spectral law
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and scalar measures $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). For a unit vector $\psi\in H$ write $\mu^{A}_{\psi}:=\mu^{A}_{T_{\psi,\psi}}$ for the scalar law of the pure state $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b). Then:

(a) **Second moment.** $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2}$ if $\psi\in D(A)$, and the integral equals $+\infty$ if $\psi\notin D(A)$; thus the second moment of the scalar law is finite exactly on $D(A)$.

(b) **Mean.** $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ if and only if $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$; in that case the mean $m(\psi):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)$ is finite and real, and if $\psi\in D(A)$ then $m(\psi)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$.

(c) **Variance.** If $\psi\in D(A)$ and $m:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, then
$$\int_{\mathbb R}(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-m^{2}=\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}\ge0 ;$$
if in addition $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, that is $\psi\in D(A)$ and $A\psi\in D(A)$, then $\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}$.

(d) **States.** Let $\rho$ be a density operator with expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. Then for every Borel function $g\ge0$
$$\int_{\mathbb R}g\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int_{\mathbb R}g\,dE_{A,u_n}\in[0,\infty],$$
so the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then it equals $\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$; the second moment satisfies $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\|Au_n\|^{2}$, with the convention that a term is $+\infty$ when $u_n\notin D(A)$, and is finite if and only if $u_n\in D(A)$ for every $n$ with $w_n>0$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]); a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; a self-adjoint operator $A$ with PVM $E_A$; a unit vector $\psi\in H$; a density operator $\rho$ with expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$.

[F1] **Spectral domain and calculus.** $D(A)=\{\psi\in H:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ and $A\psi=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)\psi$ on $D(A)$; for every Borel $f$ the operator $f(A)$ has domain $D(f(A))=\{\psi:\int|f|^{2}\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ and satisfies $\|f(A)\psi\|^{2}=\int|f|^{2}\,dE_{A,\psi}$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]],).

[F2] **Mean and second moment of a pure state.** For a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ one has $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,\psi}=\|A\psi\|^{2}$; moreover $\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (c)).

[F3] **Scalar law and its series form.** For the density operator $\rho$ with the displayed expansion and every PVM $E$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^{2}$ for every Borel $B$, and for a unit vector $u$ the law of $T_{u,u}$ is $\|E(B)u\|^{2}=E_{u}(B)$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F4] **Monotone convergence and approximation.** If $0\le f_m\uparrow f$ pointwise then $\int f_m\,d\nu\uparrow\int f\,d\nu$ for every measure $\nu$ ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]); every nonnegative measurable $g$ is the pointwise increasing limit of nonnegative simple functions ; and if $f_m\to f$ pointwise with $|f_m|\le G$ for an integrable $G$ then $\int f_m\,d\nu\to\int f\,d\nu$ ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

[F5] **Self-adjoint quadratic forms are real.** For a self-adjoint $A$ and $\psi\in D(A)$ one has $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle=\overline{\langle\psi,A\psi\rangle}=\overline{\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle}\in\mathbb R$, and $\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}=\|A\psi\|^{2}-2m\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle+m^{2}\| \psi\|^{2}$ for real $m$ ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]).

## Proof

1.1 [Second moment and mean for a state vector] Let $\psi\in H$ be a unit vector and identify $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ with the finite measure $E_{A,\psi}$. If $\psi\in D(A)$, [F1] and [F2] give $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\|A\psi\|^{2}<\infty$ and $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$; if $\psi\notin D(A)$, then [F1] gives $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\infty$, so the second moment is infinite. In the first case [F5] makes $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ real. This proves (a) and the mean formula of (b). [given, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

1.2 [Reduction of state moments to pure moments] By [F3], $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\sum_nw_nE_{A,u_n}(B)$ for every Borel $B$. Let $g\ge0$ be Borel. For indicators $g=\mathbf 1_B$ the identity $\int g\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int g\,dE_{A,u_n}$ is exactly [F3]; it extends to nonnegative simple $g$ by linearity, and to all nonnegative Borel $g$ by writing $g$ as an increasing pointwise limit of nonnegative simple functions [F4] and applying monotone convergence twice, to the measure $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and to the partial sums of the series. This proves the displayed identity of (d). [given, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [The first moment criterion] By [F2], $\int|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean is finite; conversely if $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ the integral of $|\lambda|$ diverges, so the mean is not a finite real number. Together with step 1.1 this proves (b). [given, step 1.1, F2, algebra]

2.2 [Variance of a state vector] Let $\psi\in D(A)$ be a unit vector and $m:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, a real number by [F5]. Then $A\psi-m\psi\in H$ and by [F1] applied to $f(\lambda)=\lambda-m$, $\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}=\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,dE_{A,\psi}$. Expanding the square and using [F2] for the integrals of $\lambda^{2}$, $\lambda$ and $1$ gives $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}-2m\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}+m^{2}=\|A\psi\|^{2}-2m^{2}+m^{2}=\|A\psi\|^{2}-m^{2}$. [given, step 1.1, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

3.1 [The second identity for the variance] If moreover $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, then $A\psi\in D(A)$ and the inner product $\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle$ is defined and equals $\langle A(A\psi),\psi\rangle=\langle A\psi,A\psi\rangle=\|A\psi\|^{2}$ because $A$ is self-adjoint; substituting this into step 2.2 gives $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-m^{2}=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}$, which together with step 2.2 proves (c). [step 2.2, F1, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Moments of a state] With $g=|\lambda|$ in step 1.2, the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite exactly when $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$; in that case applying the signed version of the identity to the positive and negative parts and subtracting gives $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$, using dominated convergence [F4] for the tail sums. With $g=\lambda^{2}$, step 1.2 and [F2] give $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}=\sum_nw_n\|Au_n\|^{2}$ where each term is $+\infty$ exactly when $u_n\notin D(A)$ by step 1.1; the series is finite if and only if every term of positive weight is finite. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F2, F4, algebra] ∎

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1 and Chapter 3, printed pages 55-58 and 87-100 (expectation values, spectral measures and the domain criterion of the first moment)
D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 3.3.1, printed pages 79-81 (expectation values from the spectral decomposition and the position and momentum means)

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables', Sections 1-3, printed pages 1-12 (expectation values, variances and their computation in finite and continuous examples)

items.title: Distinct density operators are separated by the law of a bounded rank-one projection
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); the Axiom of Choice is used only where the spectral theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators is invoked ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H$ with $\rho\ne\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Then:

(a) There is a unit vector $w\in H$ with $\langle\rho w,w\rangle\ne\langle\sigma w,w\rangle$.

(b) For the rank-one orthogonal projection $P:=T_{w,w}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]), whose spectral projection-valued measure assigns $P$ to the Borel set $\{1\}$, the two scalar laws of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b) satisfy
$$\mu^{P}_{\rho}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)=\langle\rho w,w\rangle,\qquad \mu^{P}_{\sigma}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P)=\langle\sigma w,w\rangle,$$
so the bounded sharp observable $P$ assigns different outcome probabilities to $\rho$ and $\sigma$.

(c) For every unit vector $w$ and every self-adjoint trace-class $T$ one has $|\operatorname{tr}(TT_{w,w})|\le\|T\|_1$; in particular $|\langle\rho w,w\rangle-\langle\sigma w,w\rangle|\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and, for the spectral PVM of clause (b), the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on $H$; unit vectors $w\in H$.

[F1] **Rank-one calculus.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ defines a trace-class operator with $\|T_{u,v}\|_1=\|u\|\,\|v\|$ and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$; $T_{u,u}$ is self-adjoint and positive with $\langle T_{u,u}x,x\rangle=|\langle x,u\rangle|^{2}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

[F2] **One-dimensional projections.** For $u\in S(H)$ the operator $T_{u,u}$ is the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto the one-dimensional subspace $\mathbb Cu$; in particular $T_{u,u}^{2}=T_{u,u}=T_{u,u}^{*}$ ([[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]], [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]).

[F3] **Density operators and their law.** A density operator $\tau$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\tau=1$, and admits an expansion $\tau=\sum_nt_nT_{v_n,v_n}$ with $t_n\ge0$, $\sum_nt_n=1$ and $(v_n)$ orthonormal; for every PVM $E$, $B\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\tau E(B))$ is a probability measure with $\operatorname{tr}(\tau E(B))=\sum_nt_n\|E(B)v_n\|^{2}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F4] **Trace ideal and trace bounds.** Products of a trace-class operator with a bounded operator are trace class and $\|ATB\|_1\le\|A\|\,\|T\|_1\|B\|$; the trace is linear on trace-class operators with $|\operatorname{tr}S|\le\|S\|_1$ ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clause 2, [[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]] clause 4).

[F5] **Quadratic form and norm.** For a bounded self-adjoint $T$ one has $\|T\|=\sup\{\,|\langle Tx,x\rangle|:\|x\|=1\,\}$, and the value is $0$ exactly when $T=0$ ([[lem-norm-of-a-self-adjoint-operator-from-its-quadratic-form]]).

[F6] **Spectral PVM of a projection.** Every orthogonal projection $P$ is a self-adjoint operator with $0\le P\le I$; by the spectral theorem it has a unique regular PVM $E_P$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ with $P=\int\lambda\,dE_P(\lambda)$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

## Proof

1.1 [Quadratic forms separate trace-class states] Put $T:=\rho-\sigma$, a nonzero self-adjoint trace-class operator by [F3] and [F4]. Suppose $\langle Tw,w\rangle=0$ for every unit vector $w$; then the supremum of [F5] is $0$, so $\|T\|=0$ and $T=0$, contradicting $\rho\ne\sigma$. Hence there is a unit $w$ with $0\ne\langle(\rho-\sigma)w,w\rangle=\langle\rho w,w\rangle-\langle\sigma w,w\rangle$, proving (a). [given, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

1.2 [The trace pairing of a rank-one projection] Let $\tau=\sum_nt_nT_{v_n,v_n}$ be the expansion of a density operator and let $w$ be a unit vector. For each $n$, the product rule $T_{v_n,v_n}T_{w,w}=T_{v_n,\langle v_n,w\rangle w}$ holds by direct evaluation on any $x$: $T_{v_n,v_n}T_{w,w}x=\langle x,w\rangle\langle w,v_n\rangle v_n=T_{v_n,\langle v_n,w\rangle w}x$; hence by [F1] its trace is $\langle v_n,\langle v_n,w\rangle w\rangle=|\langle v_n,w\rangle|^{2}$. Multiplying by $t_n$, summing and using the trace ideal and trace bound [F4] together with $\sum_nt_n\|v_n\|^{2}\|w\|^{2}=1$ gives the absolutely convergent identity $\operatorname{tr}(\tau T_{w,w})=\sum_nt_n|\langle v_n,w\rangle|^{2}$. On the other hand $\langle\tau w,w\rangle=\sum_nt_n\langle T_{v_n,v_n}w,w\rangle=\sum_nt_n|\langle w,v_n\rangle|^{2}$ by [F1] and continuity of the pairing against the norm convergent series. Since $|\langle w,v_n\rangle|=|\langle v_n,w\rangle|$, the two series agree: $\operatorname{tr}(\tau T_{w,w})=\langle\tau w,w\rangle$ for every density operator $\tau$. [given, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [The projection separates the two states] Fix a unit $w$ with $\langle\rho w,w\rangle\ne\langle\sigma w,w\rangle$, furnished by step 1.1, and put $P:=T_{w,w}$, an orthogonal projection by [F2]. The map $E'(B):=\mathbf 1_{1\in B}P+\mathbf 1_{0\in B}(I-P)$ is a regular PVM on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ with $\int\lambda\,dE'(\lambda)=1\cdot P+0\cdot(I-P)=P$: the values are orthogonal projections with $E'(\varnothing)=0$ and $E'(\mathbb R)=I$, multiplicativity holds because $P(I-P)=0$, and countable additivity holds on the two-point space $\{0,1\}$. By uniqueness in the spectral theorem [F6], $E'$ is the spectral PVM of $P$, so $E_P(\{1\})=P$ and $\mu^{P}_{\tau}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\tau P)$ for every density operator $\tau$ by [F3]. Step 1.2 identifies these numbers as $\langle\rho w,w\rangle$ and $\langle\sigma w,w\rangle$, which differ by the choice of $w$; this proves (b). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F2, F3, F6, algebra]

3.1 [The uniform bound] Let $w$ be a unit vector and let $T$ be self-adjoint trace class. By [F2] and [F4], $\|T_{w,w}\|\le\|T_{w,w}\|_1=1$ and $|\operatorname{tr}(TT_{w,w})|\le\|TT_{w,w}\|_1\le\|T\|_1$; applying this to $T=\rho-\sigma$ and using step 1.2 gives $|\langle\rho w,w\rangle-\langle\sigma w,w\rangle|=|\operatorname{tr}((\rho-\sigma)T_{w,w})|\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$, which is (c); the existence statement of (a) and the separating probability identity of (b) are steps 1.1 and 2.1. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, F2, F4, algebra] ∎

items.title: Assigned sharp observables and the outcome law of the framework
items.statement:
**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

## Remarks

- **Mixtures versus superpositions.** The affinity of clause (b) concerns statistical mixtures with classical weights, not superpositions: a coherent superposition of two preparations is a vector combination and its outcome law is not the weighted average of the two laws. The distinction is carried by the state-space items of the preceding page.
- **No discrete basis is assumed.** Nothing in this definition asserts that $A$ has eigenvalues or a complete system of eigenvectors. The outcome law exists for every assigned self-adjoint $A$ through its spectral PVM; discrete sums are the special case of a purely atomic law.

items.physical_scope: The observable and outcome-law vocabulary of the non-relativistic quantum framework: the reading of the observable and probability postulate P2 as assigned sharp self-adjoint quantities with a declared unit, their spectral projection-valued measures, the outcome law of a preparation, the spectral-support reading of outcome sets, the conditional readings of mean and variance, and the affinity of the law under statistical mixing. This item fixes terminology and readings only: it adopts no assumption beyond P1 and P2, asserts no detector or apparatus realization, makes no joint-measurement claim, records no empirical data, and excludes the finite unsharp-effect extension of P2(iv), which belongs to the measurement-and-instruments page.

items.title: The Born outcome law: probability measure, mixtures, atoms and spectral support
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the spectral suppliers. Let $H$ be the state space assigned to a declared system, let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable of the framework with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and spectrum $\sigma(A)$, and let $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ be the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Then for every preparation $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$:

(a) **Probability measure.** $0\le\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)\le1$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\mathbb R)=1$; for pairwise disjoint Borel sets $B_n$ with union $B$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\sum_n\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B_n)$; and for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ the law is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$. The declared outcome law of the model is therefore a probability measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, not a formal weight attached to eigenvectors.

(b) **Mixtures.** If $\rho=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ is a statistical mixture of preparations with weights $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}(B)$ for every Borel $B$, the series converging absolutely: the outcome law of a mixture is the weighted average of the outcome laws, with classical weights.

(c) **Exact values.** For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ the probability of the exact value $\lambda$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(\{\lambda\}))$; it is zero for every preparation whenever $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it equals the trace weight of the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)$, with $\mu^{A}_{T_{u,u}}(\{\lambda\})=1$ for every unit eigenvector $u$.

(d) **Spectral support.** $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$: outcomes outside the spectrum of the observable have probability zero.

(e) **No density and no discreteness are asserted.** The postulate asserts that $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets and does not assert that it is a density with respect to Lebesgue measure or a finite or countable sum of point masses; the operational object named there is the probability of a declared Borel set, such as a finite-resolution bin, not the value of a density at a point ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] clause (iii)). Which structure a particular pair $(A,\rho)$ exhibits is a property of that pair and is not fixed by the adopted law.

(f) **What is not claimed.** No mean, variance or higher moment is asserted by this item; their existence is conditional and is treated separately. No claim is made about the joint statistics of two or more observables, about the state after the outcome, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome, or about any concrete apparatus. The statement is conditional on P1 and P2 and on the cited mathematics.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]); the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); the assigned state space $H$ with preparation class $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]; an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ with spectral PVM $E_A$ and spectrum $\sigma(A)$; preparations $\rho,\rho_n$; Borel sets $B,B_n\subseteq\mathbb R$; and the readings of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]].

[F1] **P1.** Pure preparations are the unit rays of the assigned Hilbert space, general preparations are the density operators $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, and a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ with $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$ is a preparation ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] clauses (i)-(iii), [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

[F2] **P2.** An ideal sharp real-valued quantity is a self-adjoint operator with a declared unit; its spectral PVM assigns to a Borel set $B$ the probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$, equal to $\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$ for a unit pure preparation; the law is a measure and not necessarily a density or a discrete sum; an outcome belongs to the spectral support, and an exact continuous value is not a finite-resolution record ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] clauses (i)-(iii)).

[F3] **Scalar law.** For every density operator $\rho$ with expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ and every PVM $E$, the assignment $B\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a probability measure with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^{2}$; for a unit vector $u$ it equals $\|E(B)u\|^{2}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F4] **Atoms and eigenvalues.** $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection onto $\ker(A-\lambda)$; it is nonzero exactly when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$; consequently $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(\{\lambda\}))=0$ for every preparation when $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue, and $\mu^{A}_{T_{u,u}}(\{\lambda\})=1$ for every unit eigenvector $u$ at $\lambda$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F5] **Spectral support.** $E_A(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(A))=0$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B\cap\sigma(A)))$ with $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F6] **Affinity.** For a trace-norm convergent mixture $\rho=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ of density operators one has $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\sum_nw_n\operatorname{tr}(\rho_nE_A(B))$ for every Borel set $B$, the series converging absolutely ([[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F7] **Nature of the law (P2 clause (iii)).** The postulate asserts that the outcome law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses; an exact value of a continuum quantity is an idealization, and a real detector reports the probability of a declared Borel set such as a bin ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] clause (iii)).

[F8] **Spectral theorem.** The spectral PVM $E_A$ exists, is unique among regular PVMs on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ representing $A$, and is the object whose scalar measures enter [F3] ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

## Proof

1.1 [Clause (a)] By [F2] the outcome law is defined using the spectral PVM of [F8], and by $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$; by [F3] it is a probability measure on the Borel sets with values in $[0,1]$, normalization $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\mathbb R)=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ and countable additivity, and for a unit vector $\psi$ it equals $\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$. This is clause (a). [given, F2, F3, F8, algebra]

1.2 [Clause (b)] Let $\rho=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ be a statistical mixture; by [F1] it is a preparation, and [F6] gives $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\sum_nw_n\operatorname{tr}(\rho_nE_A(B))=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}(B)$ for every Borel $B$ with absolute convergence. [given, F1, F6, algebra]

1.3 [Clause (c)] By [F4], $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection onto $\ker(A-\lambda)$ and vanishes exactly when $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue; hence $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(\{\lambda\}))=0$ for every preparation in that case, while for a unit eigenvector $u$ at $\lambda$ the same reference gives $\mu^{A}_{T_{u,u}}(\{\lambda\})=1$, and the value is the trace weight of the eigenspace. [given, F4, algebra]

1.4 [Clause (d)] By [F5], $E_A(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(A))=0$ and hence $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B\cap\sigma(A)))=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$, with $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$; this is the spectral-support reading of [F2]. [given, F5, algebra]

1.5 [Clause (e)] By [F2] the law is asserted to be a probability measure, and by [F7] the postulate neither asserts that it is a density with respect to Lebesgue measure nor that it is a finite or countable sum of point masses, the operational object being the probability of a declared Borel set. Therefore clause (e) is a reading of P2 clause (iii) alone, and no further structure of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is claimed. [given, F2, F7]

2.1 [Clause (f) and conclusion] Steps 1.1-1.4 prove clauses (a)-(d) from P1, P2 and the cited mathematics, and step 1.5 records the limits of clause (e). Nothing in the argument uses moments, joint statistics, state updates, apparatus models or data, so none of these is claimed. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 1.5] ∎

The item is conditional on P1 and P2 and on the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem; it asserts nothing about concrete apparatuses, joint measurements, moments, state updates or empirical data.

items.title: Mean, second moment and variance of an assigned observable in a preparation
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$; the second moment is $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\|Au_n\|^{2}\in[0,\infty]$, finite if and only if $u_n\in D(A)$ for every $n$ of positive weight. More generally the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] shows that whenever the means are finite the mean of a statistical mixture is the weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]); the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ with spectral law $\mu^{A}$ and declared unit $u_A$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; a unit vector $\psi$; a preparation $\rho$ with spectral expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).

[F1] **The outcome law.** For an assigned observable the preparation-dependent law is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$, equal to $\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$ for a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$, and $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (b) and (c), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] clause (a)).

[F2] **Moments of the scalar law.** For a unit vector $\psi$: the second moment satisfies $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\|A\psi\|^{2}$ if $\psi\in D(A)$ and equals $+\infty$ otherwise; the mean satisfies $\int|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and is then finite and real with $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ for $\psi\in D(A)$; for $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance is $\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|^{2}$, and for $\psi\in D(A^{2})$ it is $\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F3] **Mixtures.** For preparations $\rho_n$ with weights $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, the mixture $\rho=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ is a preparation and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}(B)$ for every Borel $B$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b), clauses (b) and (d)).

[F4] **State moments of a mixture.** For a density operator with expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite exactly when $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$ and is then $\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$, while $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\|Au_n\|^{2}\in[0,\infty]$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]] clause (d)).

[F5] **Preparations and domains.** A preparation is a unit ray of the assigned Hilbert space or a density operator on it; being a preparation imposes no membership in $D(A)$ or $D(A^{2})$ beyond what is stated for the assigned observable $A$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] clauses (a)-(c), [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] clauses (ii)-(iii)).

## Proof

1.1 [Clause (a): mean and second moment of a pure preparation] Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. By [F1] the law of the preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$; by [F2] its second moment is $\|A\psi\|^{2}$ if $\psi\in D(A)$ (and $+\infty$ otherwise), and its mean is $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ when $\psi\in D(A)$; when $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, [F2] gives the displayed variance value. This proves (a). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Clause (c): domains and non-existence] By [F2], $\int|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is finite exactly for $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean is finite; if $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ the integral of $|\lambda|$ diverges and no finite mean exists, while $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\infty$ whenever $\psi\notin D(A)$. Membership of $\psi$ in these domains is not implied by being a preparation: [F5] says only that preparations are unit rays or density operators. [given, F2, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (b): variance under the single hypothesis $\psi\in D(A)$] Let $\psi\in D(A)$ be a unit vector. By [F2] the variance equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}$ and also $\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}$ with $m=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, a real number because $A$ is self-adjoint; this squared norm is nonnegative, so the variance exists, is finite and is nonnegative, and no eigenbasis or additional domain hypothesis is used. [given, step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [Clause (d): mixtures] Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be the spectral expansion. By [F4] the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite exactly when $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$ and then has the displayed value, and $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\|Au_n\|^{2}$. The mixture identity for the law itself is [F3]; taking $g=|\lambda|$ and $\lambda^{2}$ in the series identity of [F4] and combining with [F2] yields the stated criteria, and when all mean terms are finite the weighted average is the mean of the mixture. [given, step 1.1, step 2.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Clause (e) and conclusion] Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1 prove (a)-(d) as conditional statements from P1, P2 and the cited mathematics; the reminders recorded in (e) are visible in the hypotheses of those steps, and no apparatus, error, disturbance or empirical claim enters the argument. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎
