items.physical_scope: Conditional statements, within the framework's observable and probability postulate, about the mean and second central moment of the outcome law of an assigned sharp observable in a preparation: for a pure preparation of a unit vector in the domain of the observable the mean and second moment are the quadratic form and the squared norm; the variance is the squared norm of the centred vector; the mean is finite exactly when the state lies in the domain of the square root of the modulus; a preparation need not lie in the domain of the observable, so moments are not automatic; and for a statistical mixture the moments are the weighted averages when finite. The item asserts no apparatus error, no disturbance and no empirical result.

items.title: Position and momentum outcome laws and the Born density of the massive particle model
items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] (P5) for a spinless particle of mass $m>0$ and action constant $\hbar>0$, with state space $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ as in [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]), and for a unit vector $\psi\in H$ let $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}$ and $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}$ be the outcome laws of the assigned observables $Q_{j}$ and $P_{j}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Then:

(a) **Position observable.** $Q_{j}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(Q_{j})=\{\psi\in H:x_{j}\psi\in H\}$, its spectral PVM is given by $E_{Q_{j}}(B)\psi=\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\psi$, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}).$$
The law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure with density
$$f_{j}(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi(x_{\perp},t)|^{2}\,dx_{\perp},$$
the $j$-th marginal density of $|\psi|^{2}$, and it is atomless: $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Moreover $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$.

(b) **Joint position law.** There is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}\subseteq\mathbb R$, and its scalar law in the preparation $\psi$ is the measure of the density $|\psi|^{2}$:
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}\ \text{Borel}).$$
Thus the model's position law in a spatial region $B$ is $\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$: the Born density $|\psi|^{2}$ is the joint outcome density of the three commuting position observables.

(c) **Momentum observable.** $P_{j}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(P_{j})=\{\psi\in H:\xi_{j}\mathcal F_{2}\psi\in L^{2}\}$ and Fourier representation $\mathcal F_{2}(P_{j}\psi)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{j}\,\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)$; its spectral PVM is $E_{P_{j}}(B)=\mathcal F_{2}^{-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}\mathcal F_{2}$ with $m(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}$, and
$$\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)|^{2}\,d\xi,\qquad m^{-1}(B)=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^{3}:2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}\in B\}.$$
The law is absolutely continuous with density
$$g_{j}(p)=\frac{1}{2\pi\hbar}\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}\bigl|\mathcal F_{2}\psi\bigl(\xi_{\perp},\tfrac{p}{2\pi\hbar}\bigr)\bigr|^{2}d\xi_{\perp}$$
in the momentum variable $p$, and it is atomless; moreover $\sigma(P_{j})=\mathbb R$.

(d) **Exact values.** For every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ one has $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ and $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every preparation, although both observables have spectrum $\mathbb R$: an exact position or momentum value is not an outcome of the model's sharp law, while its finite-resolution readings are the Borel bin probabilities of (a)-(c).

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, on the massive spinless model of P5 and on the cited mathematics. The componentwise extension to the spin-$s$ model is not proved here; no joint statistics of a position and a momentum observable, no dynamics and no apparatus or empirical claim are made. The identification of the operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ with concrete laboratory position and momentum measurements is a tested identification under P7 and is not asserted by this item.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P2 and P5 for a spinless particle of mass $m>0$ with state space $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]); the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); the operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]]; the Plancherel transform $\mathcal F_{2}$ of [[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]] and [[thm-plancherel]]; a unit vector $\psi\in H$; Borel sets $B,B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}$; and the outcome-law reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]].

[F1] **Outcome law of an assigned observable.** For an assigned observable $A$ and a unit vector $\psi$ the law is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$, where $E_{A}$ is the spectral PVM of $A$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (b) and (c), clause (ii)).

[F2] **The massive-particle model.** P5 assigns the state space $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ to a spinless particle of mass $m>0$ and defines $(Q_{j}\psi)(x)=x_{j}\psi(x)$ on the classes with $x_{j}\psi\in L^{2}$ and $(P_{k}\psi)=-i\hbar D_{k}\psi$ on the classes whose componentwise weak derivative lies in $L^{2}$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] clause (iii)).

[F3] **Self-adjointness and Fourier representation.** $Q_{j}$ is self-adjoint with $D(Q_{j})=\{\psi:x_{j}\psi\in L^{2}\}$; $P_{j}$ is self-adjoint with $D(P_{j})=\{\psi:\xi_{j}\mathcal F_{2}\psi\in L^{2}\}$ and $\mathcal F_{2}(P_{j}\psi)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)$ almost everywhere ([[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum-operators-self-adjoint]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F4] **Multiplication operators.** Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space and $m:X\to\mathbb R$ measurable and finite $\mu$-a.e.; then $M_{m}f=mf$ on $D(M_{m})=\{f:\int|m|^{2}|f|^{2}d\mu<\infty\}$ is self-adjoint with regular spectral PVM $E(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$, $\int\lambda\,dE=M_{m}$ and $\sigma(M_{m})$ equal to the essential range of $m$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-l2-multiplication-spectral-measure]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F5] **Unitary transport of a spectral PVM.** If $U$ is unitary and $F$ is a regular PVM, then $B\mapsto U^{-1}F(B)U$ is a regular PVM with $U^{-1}(\int\lambda\,dF(\lambda))U=\int\lambda\,d(U^{-1}FU)(\lambda)$ on the transported domain; the spectral PVM of a self-adjoint operator is the unique regular PVM representing it, so a transported regular PVM representing the transported operator is its spectral PVM ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

[F6] **Tonelli, null sets and indefinite integrals.** For $\sigma$-finite measure spaces, integrals of product-measurable nonnegative functions may be iterated ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]); for nonnegative measurable $f$ the set function $A\mapsto\int_{A}f\,d\mu$ is a measure ([[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]]); countable subsets of $\mathbb R^{n}$ are Lebesgue-null ([[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]).

[F7] **Measure uniqueness on a pi-system.** Finite measures on the $\sigma$-algebra generated by a $\pi$-system that agree on the $\pi$-system and have equal total mass are equal ([[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]]); the Euclidean Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R^{3}$ is generated by the rectangles $B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3}$ ([[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]],).

## Proof

1.1 [The position observable] On the $\sigma$-finite space $(\mathbb R^{3},\text{Borel},\text{Lebesgue})$ the function $x\mapsto x_{j}$ is real, measurable and finite everywhere, so [F4] applies to $M_{x_{j}}$; by [F2] and [F3] the operator $Q_{j}$ is exactly $M_{x_{j}}$ with its displayed domain, hence is self-adjoint with spectral PVM $E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}$ and $\sigma(Q_{j})$, the essential range of $x_{j}$, equal to $\mathbb R$ (every open interval in the $j$-th coordinate has a slab preimage of positive Lebesgue measure). For a unit vector $\psi$, [F1] gives $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}|\psi(x)|^{2}dx$. Writing the integral over $x_{j}^{-1}(B)=\{(x_{\perp},t):t\in B\}$ as an iterated integral by Tonelli [F6] identifies the density $f_{j}(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi(x_{\perp},t)|^{2}dx_{\perp}$: $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}f_{j}(t)\,dt$. For the atomless claim, $x_{j}^{-1}(\{\lambda\})$ is a translate of $\mathbb R^{2}$, and the integral over $t\in\{\lambda\}$ vanishes because $\{\lambda\}$ is countable hence Lebesgue-null [F6]; equivalently $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=\int_{\{\lambda\}}f_{j}(t)dt=0$. This is clause (a). [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, algebra]

1.2 [The momentum observable] By [F3] the operator $P_{j}$ is self-adjoint with the stated domain and Fourier representation. Let $M:=M_{2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}}$ be the multiplication operator of [F4] on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with multiplier $m(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}$, whose spectral PVM is $E^{M}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$; then $P_{j}=\mathcal F_{2}^{-1}M\mathcal F_{2}$ on $D(P_{j})=\mathcal F_{2}^{-1}D(M)$ by [F3], so by the transport rule [F5] the operator family $E_{P_{j}}(B):=\mathcal F_{2}^{-1}E^{M}(B)\mathcal F_{2}$ is a regular PVM representing $P_{j}$; since the spectral PVM is unique among regular PVMs representing a self-adjoint operator, $E_{P_{j}}$ is the spectral PVM of $P_{j}$ and $\sigma(P_{j})=\sigma(M)=\mathbb R$ is the essential range of $2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}$. For a unit $\psi$, [F1] and unitarity of $\mathcal F_{2}$ give $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{P_{j}}(B)\psi\|^{2}=\|E^{M}(B)\mathcal F_{2}\psi\|^{2}=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)|^{2}d\xi$. Substituting the momentum variable $p=2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}$ and iterating the resulting integral by Tonelli [F6] gives the density $g_{j}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi_{\perp},p/(2\pi\hbar))|^{2}d\xi_{\perp}$; the atomless claim follows because $m^{-1}(\{p\})$ lies in a hyperplane, which is a countable union of Lebesgue-null sets [F6] and hence has zero $|\mathcal F_{2}\psi|^{2}$-measure. This is clause (c). [given, F1, F3, F4, F5, F6, algebra]

2.1 [The joint position law] Define $G(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$ for Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, the multiplication operator by the indicator of $B$: by [F4] applied to the multiplier $x\mapsto x$ (or directly to the indicator multipliers) $G$ is a regular PVM on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R^{3}$, and $G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=M_{\mathbf 1_{B_{1}}(x_{1})\mathbf 1_{B_{2}}(x_{2})\mathbf 1_{B_{3}}(x_{3})}=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$ by step 1.1, since multiplication operators commute. For a unit $\psi$ the scalar law is $\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}dx$, which is a measure on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R^{3}$ by [F6]. If $H$ is another regular PVM with the same values on all rectangles, then for every unit $\varphi$ the finite measures $B\mapsto\langle H(B)\varphi,\varphi\rangle$ and $B\mapsto\langle G(B)\varphi,\varphi\rangle$ agree on rectangles, which form a $\pi$-system generating the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R^{3}$ by [F7], and have the common total mass $\|\varphi\|^{2}$; [F7] makes them equal on all Borel sets, and the polarization identity recovers $\langle H(B)\varphi,\psi\rangle=\langle G(B)\varphi,\psi\rangle$ for all $\varphi,\psi$, so $H=G$. Hence $G$ is the unique regular PVM with the displayed rectangle values, and the law of every preparation in the joint position observable is the measure of $|\psi|^{2}$: clause (b). [step 1.1, F1, F4, F6, F7, algebra]

3.1 [Exact values and conclusion] Clause (d) is the atomless statement of steps 1.1 and 1.2 combined with the spectral-support reading of the outcome law, which places outcomes in the spectra $\sigma(Q_{j})=\sigma(P_{j})=\mathbb R$ computed there; no finite-resolution reading is affected, since the bin probabilities remain those of (a)-(c). Steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 prove clauses (a)-(c) from P2, P5 and the cited mathematics, and the hypotheses recorded in (e) are exactly those used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, F1, algebra] ∎

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.2 and Section 3.1, printed pages 58-69 and 88-95 (position and momentum operators, multiplication operators and their spectral measures)

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 \"Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation\", Section 3, printed pages 11-15 (position and momentum states, their inner products and the interpretation of the wave function)

items.physical_scope: Conditional consequences of the adopted observable and probability postulate for the spinless massive-particle model of the kinematics postulate: the position operators are self-adjoint with their maximal domains and have spectral outcome laws with the density |psi|^2; the three position observables possess a unique joint spectral measure whose law in a preparation is the measure of |psi|^2, so the Born density is the model's position law; the momentum operators are self-adjoint with their Fourier multipliers and have outcome laws with density |psi-hat|^2 in the momentum variable; exact values of position and momentum have probability zero for every preparation although both spectra are all of R. The item is spinless, asserts no joint position-momentum statistics, no dynamics and no empirical result.

items.title: Distinct preparations are separated by the statistics of a bounded sharp observable
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be the state space assigned to a declared system and let $\rho\ne\sigma$ be two preparations of the system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] clauses (a)-(c). Then there is a bounded sharp observable of the framework, namely an orthogonal projection $P$ of rank one, such that the outcome laws of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] differ at the outcome set $\{1\}$:
$$\mu^{P}_{\rho}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)\ne\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P)=\mu^{P}_{\sigma}(\{1\}).$$
Moreover for every rank-one projection $P$ one has $|\mu^{P}_{\rho}(\{1\})-\mu^{P}_{\sigma}(\{1\})|\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_{1}$; consequently, if $\mu^{P}_{\rho}=\mu^{P}_{\sigma}$ for every bounded sharp observable $P$ (or merely for every rank-one projection), then $\rho=\sigma$.

The statement is conditional on P1 and P2 and asserts no procedure that determines a preparation from finitely many measurements, no apparatus realization, no error rate and no empirical result.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]); the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); the assigned state space $H$ with preparation class of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]; preparations $\rho,\sigma$ with $\rho\ne\sigma$.

[F1] **Mathematical separation.** For distinct density operators $\rho,\sigma$ there is a unit vector $w\in H$ with $\langle\rho w,w\rangle\ne\langle\sigma w,w\rangle$; for the rank-one projection $P=T_{w,w}$ the spectral law of $P$ satisfies $\mu^{P}_{\rho}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)=\langle\rho w,w\rangle$ and likewise for $\sigma$, and $|\operatorname{tr}((\rho-\sigma)T_{w,w})|\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_{1}$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-states-separated-by-bounded-projections]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] **The framework's outcome law and its reading.** An assigned sharp observable has spectral PVM $E_A$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$, equal to $\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$ for a pure preparation; the law is a probability measure on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$, and the outcome-set reading of the model is that of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] clauses (a)-(c), clause (ii)).

[F3] **Projections are assigned bounded observables.** An orthogonal projection $P$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator with $0\le P\le I$ on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]), hence qualifies as a sharp observable of the framework when assigned with the dimensionless unit of its spectral coordinate.

## Proof

1.1 [Existence of a separating bounded observable] Let $w$ and $P=T_{w,w}$ be as in [F1]: such a unit vector exists because $\rho\ne\sigma$ and $\rho-\sigma$ is a nonzero self-adjoint trace-class operator. By [F3] the operator $P$ is a bounded self-adjoint projection, hence an assigned sharp observable of the framework once its unit (the dimensionless spectral coordinate, which here takes the values $0$ and $1$) is declared; its spectral law at $\{1\}$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P)$ by [F2], and [F1] gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)=\langle\rho w,w\rangle\ne\langle\sigma w,w\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P)$. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Uniform bound and separation] The bound $|\mu^{P}_{\rho}(\{1\})-\mu^{P}_{\sigma}(\{1\})|=|\operatorname{tr}((\rho-\sigma)P)|\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_{1}$ is [F1] applied to the rank-one projection $P$. If all rank-one projections have equal laws for $\rho$ and $\sigma$, then $\langle\rho w,w\rangle=\langle\sigma w,w\rangle$ for every unit $w$ by the same identification, contradicting the choice of $w$ in [F1] unless $\rho=\sigma$; hence statistical identity for all such observables forces the preparations to coincide. This proves the statement, and the assertion involves no measurement procedure beyond the model's outcome law. [step 1.1, given, F1, F2, algebra] ∎

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.3, printed pages 121-126 (the density operator and the trace rule, with distinct states having different statistics)

items.physical_scope: A conditional separation statement for the framework's preparations: two distinct preparations of a declared system assign different probabilities to some outcome of some bounded sharp observable of the framework, namely to the outcome 1 of a rank-one orthogonal projection; the difference is bounded by the trace-norm distance of the two states. The item asserts no finite-measurement procedure that identifies a preparation, no apparatus realization and no empirical result; it concerns the model's state space under the state and observable postulates.

items.title: What the observable and Born-probability page adopts, proves and does not claim
items.statement:
**Adopted, not restated.** The physical content of this page is the observable and probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), read in the vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]: assigning to a declared system a self-adjoint operator with a declared unit, its spectral projection-valued measure, and the outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$. The page adopts no further physical assumption; the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem are carried explicitly, and the position and momentum statements are conditional on the massive-particle model postulate P5 as read through the magnetic-and-detection operator definitions.

**What is proved.** [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] identifies the atoms of the spectral measure with the eigenspace projections, so that an exact value has zero probability unless it is an eigenvalue. [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] identifies the support of the spectral measure with the spectrum, giving the precise reading of the statement that an outcome lies in the spectrum. [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] proves affinity under statistical mixtures and uniform trace-norm continuity. [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]] assembles the mean, second moment and variance formulas with their exact domain criteria, and [[lem-nrqm-observables-states-separated-by-bounded-projections]] proves that distinct states are separated by the law of a rank-one projection. The physics theorems read these results as conditional statements about assigned observables: [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] (the law is a probability measure, affine in mixtures, atomic only at eigenvalues, supported in the spectrum and not assumed to have a density), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] (moments exist exactly under the stated domain hypotheses), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-position-and-momentum-outcome-laws]] (the position and momentum laws of the spinless massive model with densities $|\psi|^{2}$ and $|\mathcal F_2\psi|^{2}$, and the joint position measure) and [[pthm-nrqm-observables-states-separated-by-born-statistics]] (distinct preparations differ in some bounded observable's statistics).

**No complete eigenbasis.** Following the correction recorded in the source audit, the page never asserts that a general self-adjoint operator has a complete discrete system of eigenvectors. The spectral projection-valued measure replaces the eigenbasis; discrete sums are the special case of an atomic law, and continuous parts are handled through measures. The expectation formula $\langle\hat O\rangle=\langle\psi,\hat O\psi\rangle$ is proved here only for $\psi$ in the domain of the operator and through the spectral integral, not through an assumed eigenfunction expansion.

**What is not claimed.** No item of this page asserts an apparatus realization of any observable, a joint measurement of two observables, a state update after an outcome, a density for an arbitrary outcome law, the existence of a mean or variance for an arbitrary preparation, a measured value or a comparison with data. The finite unsharp-effect extension of P2(iv) and all instrument content belong to the measurement-and-instruments page, the componentwise spin extension of the position and momentum laws belongs to the kinematics page, and the identification of concrete laboratory procedures with assigned observables is a tested identification under P7, not a consequence of the postulates. Agreement of the conditional predictions with data would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions; it is not established or claimed here.

It proves nothing and reports no observation.

items.title: An exact two-level energy readout and its moments
items.statement:
Let $H=\mathbb C^{2}$ carry the standard inner product $\langle z,w\rangle=z_{1}\overline{w_{1}}+z_{2}\overline{w_{2}}$ ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]), with orthonormal basis $e_{1}=(1,0)$, $e_{2}=(0,1)$. Fix two distinct energies $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$ in joules (model parameters, not measured values), and consider the assigned sharp observable
$$A:=E_{1}T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+E_{2}T_{e_{2},e_{2}},\qquad u_{A}=\mathrm J,$$
with $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ the rank-one calculus of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Then:

(i) $A$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $D(A)=H$; its spectral projection-valued measure is
$$E_{A}(B)=\mathbf 1_{E_{1}\in B}\,T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+\mathbf 1_{E_{2}\in B}\,T_{e_{2},e_{2}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
so the spectrum is $\sigma(A)=\{E_{1},E_{2}\}$ and every outcome lies in it.

(ii) For the pure preparation of the unit vector $\psi=c_{1}e_{1}+c_{2}e_{2}$, $|c_{1}|^{2}+|c_{2}|^{2}=1$, the outcome law is
$$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\{E_{1}\})=|c_{1}|^{2},\qquad \mu^{A}_{\psi}(\{E_{2}\})=|c_{2}|^{2},\qquad \mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\sum_{i:E_{i}\in B}|c_{i}|^{2},$$
and for the mixed preparation $\rho=w\,T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+(1-w)T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ with $0\le w\le1$ the law is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{E_{1}\})=w$, $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{E_{2}\})=1-w$.

(iii) With $p:=|c_{1}|^{2}$ and $q:=|c_{2}|^{2}=1-p$, the mean, second moment and variance of the pure preparation are
$$\langle E\rangle_{\psi}=E_{1}p+E_{2}q,\qquad \langle E^{2}\rangle_{\psi}=E_{1}^{2}p+E_{2}^{2}q,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_{\psi}=pq\,(E_{1}-E_{2})^{2},$$
and for the mixture $pq$ is replaced by $w(1-w)$; all three numbers are finite and exact because $A$ is bounded.

The computation is a model-internal readout: the $E_{i}$ are parameters of the assigned observable, the probabilities are those of the framework's outcome law, and no laboratory measurement, apparatus or empirical value is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Hilbert space $H=\mathbb C^{2}$ with the standard inner product and orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$; distinct real energies $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$ in joules; the assigned observable $A=E_{1}T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+E_{2}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ with unit $\mathrm J$; a unit vector $\psi=c_{1}e_{1}+c_{2}e_{2}$; a weight $w\in[0,1]$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers.

[F1] **Rank-one calculus and one-dimensional projections.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is linear in $x$, with $T_{u,v}^{*}=T_{v,u}$ and $T_{u,u}$ self-adjoint and positive; for unit $u$ the operator $T_{u,u}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb Cu$ with $T_{u,u}^{2}=T_{u,u}$, and for orthonormal $u,v$ one has $T_{u,u}T_{v,v}=0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]], [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]],).

[F2] **Finite-dimensional spectral structure.** The eigenvectors $e_{1},e_{2}$ of the normal operator $A$ form an orthonormal basis of $H$, so $T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+T_{e_{2},e_{2}}=I$ ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]).

[F3] **Spectral PVM uniqueness.** A self-adjoint operator has a unique regular PVM on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ representing it, and the spectral PVM is that measure ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

[F4] **Outcome law.** For an assigned observable the law is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$, equal to $\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ for a pure preparation, and it is affine under mixtures ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (b) and (c), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F5] **Moments.** For a unit vector in $D(A)$ the mean and second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$, and the variance is the second moment minus the square of the mean (clauses (a)-(c), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F6] **States of the model.** A pure preparation is the state $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of a unit vector; a convex combination of states with weights is a state, and its trace is the corresponding convex combination of traces ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], clause (a)).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the spectral measure, the outcome probabilities and the moments on the explicit two-dimensional data.

1.1 [The observable and its spectral measure] $A=E_{1}T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+E_{2}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ is bounded with $\|A\|\le\max\{|E_{1}|,|E_{2}|\}$ and self-adjoint because each $T_{e_{i},e_{i}}$ is self-adjoint by [F1] and $E_{i}\in\mathbb R$; $Ae_{1}=E_{1}e_{1}$ and $Ae_{2}=E_{2}e_{2}$. Define $E'(B):=\mathbf 1_{E_{1}\in B}T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+\mathbf 1_{E_{2}\in B}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$; [F1] gives that each value is an orthogonal projection and that $T_{e_{1},e_{1}}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}=T_{e_{2},e_{2}}T_{e_{1},e_{1}}=0$, while [F2] gives $E'(\mathbb R)=I$; multiplicativity and countable additivity hold because the two-point space $\{E_{1},E_{2}\}$ is finite, and the integral of the identity against $E'$ is $E_{1}T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+E_{2}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}=A$. By uniqueness [F3], $E'$ is the spectral PVM of $A$, so $\sigma(A)=\{E_{1},E_{2}\}$ and clause (i) holds. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Outcome probabilities] For the unit vector $\psi=c_{1}e_{1}+c_{2}e_{2}$, the identity $T_{e_{i},e_{i}}\psi=\langle\psi,e_{i}\rangle e_{i}=c_{i}e_{i}$ from [F1] gives $E_{A}(B)\psi=\sum_{i:E_{i}\in B}c_{i}e_{i}$, whose norm squared is $\sum_{i:E_{i}\in B}|c_{i}|^{2}$; by [F4] this is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)$, so in particular $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\{E_{i}\})=|c_{i}|^{2}$ and the total mass is $|c_{1}|^{2}+|c_{2}|^{2}=1$. For the mixture, [F4] and linearity of the trace give $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{E_{1}\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho T_{e_{1},e_{1}})=w$ because $\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{1},e_{1}}^{2})=1$ and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{2},e_{2}}T_{e_{1},e_{1}})=0$ by [F1], and similarly $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{E_{2}\})=1-w$; this is clause (ii). [given, step 1.1, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Moments of the readout] With $p=|c_{1}|^{2}$, $q=|c_{2}|^{2}$, the vector $\psi$ lies in $D(A)=H$, so [F5] applies: the mean is $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle=E_{1}p+E_{2}q$, the second moment is $\|A\psi\|^{2}=E_{1}^{2}p+E_{2}^{2}q$, and the variance is their difference, computed as $E_{1}^{2}p+E_{2}^{2}q-(E_{1}p+E_{2}q)^{2}=p(1-p)E_{1}^{2}+q(1-q)E_{2}^{2}-2pqE_{1}E_{2}=pq(E_{1}-E_{2})^{2}$, using $p+q=1$ and $[F6]$. For the mixture $\rho=wT_{e_{1},e_{1}}+(1-w)T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$, which is a state by [F6], the same identities give mean $wE_{1}+(1-w)E_{2}$ and variance $w(1-w)(E_{1}-E_{2})^{2}$, since the law is the two-point law of (ii) and the moments of a finite two-point law are the displayed sums. All quantities are finite because $A$ is bounded. This is clause (iii). [given, step 2.1, F1, F5, F6, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The two eigenvalues $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$ are distinct, so the eigenspaces are one-dimensional and the spectral projections are exactly the rank-one projections $T_{e_{i},e_{i}}$; a degenerate energy would replace them by the projection onto the eigenspace and the exact-value probabilities by its trace weight, in agreement with [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]].
- The example is a finite model computation, not a reported experiment: nothing here identifies $E_{1},E_{2}$ with the levels of a specific physical system, and no counts, uncertainty or apparatus behaviour is asserted.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Section 1, printed pages 1-6 (the two-state Hamiltonian with energies g_0 plus or minus g and its energy eigenstates)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 1.3.6 and 2.1, printed pages 13-14 and 17-21 (probabilities in a two-state space and the operator description of observables)

items.physical_scope: A finite, exact model computation in the two-level state space of the framework: the energy observable E_1 P_1 + E_2 P_2 for two distinct energies in joules, its spectral measure, the outcome probabilities of a pure and of a mixed preparation, and the mean, second moment and variance of the readout. The energies are model parameters; the item asserts no apparatus realization, no measurement statistics from a laboratory and no empirical value.

items.title: Position-bin probabilities of a Gaussian packet
items.statement:
Work in the spinless massive-particle model of P5, that is $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with position operators $Q_{j}$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]], [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]]), fix a width $\sigma>0$ in metres, and let
$$\psi_{\sigma}(t):=(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/4}e^{-t^{2}/(4\sigma^{2})}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the **Gaussian packet** of width $\sigma$. Let $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{2};\mathbb C)$ satisfy $\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\varphi|^{2}=1$ and put
$$\psi(x):=\psi_{\sigma}(x_{1})\,\varphi(x_{2},x_{3})\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^{3}),$$
so that $\psi\in H$ is a unit vector and the preparation $[\psi]$ is a state of the model. Then:

(i) The probability that the first coordinate $Q_{1}$ lies in a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is
$$\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}\,dt=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}}\int_{B}e^{-t^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}\,dt,$$
independently of the transverse factor $\varphi$; the law has density $|\psi_{\sigma}|^{2}$ and $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}(\mathbb R)=1$.

(ii) For every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ the probability of the exact value $\lambda$ is zero, $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$, while for every $a<b$ the bin $(a,b]$ has positive probability with the explicit bounds
$$\frac{2(b-a)}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}}\exp\Bigl(-\frac{\max\{|a|,|b|\}^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\Bigr)\le\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}((a,b])\le\frac{2(b-a)}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}}$$
when $0\le a<b$, and in the symmetric case $a=-\delta$, $b=\delta$ the probability satisfies
$$\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi e}}\ \le\ \mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}((-\sigma,\sigma])\ \le\ \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}},\qquad 0\ <\ \mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}((-\delta,\delta])\ \le\ \frac{2\delta}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}}.$$
In particular a single recorded event localized in a bin of positive length is possible in the model, while an event at an exact coordinate value has probability zero.

(iii) The remaining coordinates obey the same statement with $j\in\{1,2,3\}$; for the transverse factor $\varphi$ the first-coordinate computation is independent of its detailed shape, and the numbers above are model parameters $\sigma$ and bin endpoints only, read in metres.

The computation is the framework's own outcome law applied to an explicit state; it records no measurement, no apparatus response and no empirical data.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The spinless massive-particle model of P5 with $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and position operators $Q_{j}$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]], [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]]); the outcome-law reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; a width $\sigma>0$; a unit vector $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{2};\mathbb C)$; the Gaussian packet $\psi_{\sigma}$ and state $\psi=\psi_{\sigma}\otimes\varphi$; a bin $(a,b]\subseteq\mathbb R$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] **Gaussian integrals.** $\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-u^{2}}du=\sqrt\pi$ ([[thm-gaussian-integral]]); for $c>0$ the $C^{1}$ substitution $u=t/\sqrt{2c}$ gives $\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-t^{2}/(2c)}dt=\sqrt{2\pi c}$.

[F2] **Position law of the model.** For the spinless massive model and a unit vector $\psi$, the law of $Q_{j}$ is $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}|\psi(x)|^{2}dx$, with density $f_{j}(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi(x_{\perp},t)|^{2}dx_{\perp}$ and $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every $\lambda$ ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-position-and-momentum-outcome-laws]] clauses (a) and (d), clauses (a) and (c), clauses (a) and (b)).

[F3] **Iterated integrals and monotonicity.** For product-measurable nonnegative functions on $\sigma$-finite spaces the integral may be iterated ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]); for nonnegative measurable $f\le g$ one has $\int f\le\int g$ and $\int_A f\le\int_B f$ for $A\subseteq B$, directly from the supremum definition of the nonnegative integral ([[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]); and $t\mapsto e^{-t^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}$ is continuous, hence Borel measurable ([[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]).

[F4] **The product state is a unit vector.** $\psi=\psi_{\sigma}\otimes\varphi$ is the almost-everywhere product of an $L^{2}$ function of $x_{1}$ and an $L^{2}$ function of $(x_{2},x_{3})$, hence lies in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],); Tonelli [F3] and the normalizations of $\psi_{\sigma}$ and $\varphi$ give $\|\psi\|^{2}=1$, and $|\psi|^{2}$ is the product $|\psi_{\sigma}(x_{1})|^{2}|\varphi(x_{2},x_{3})|^{2}$ because the modulus of a product is the product of the moduli ([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]).

[F5] **States.** The pure preparation of the unit vector $\psi$ is the state $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of the model, and the outcome law is read as in [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; normalize the Gaussian packet and compute the position-bin probabilities, their bounds and the exact-value probability.

1.1 [Normalization of the Gaussian packet] With $c=\sigma^{2}$ in [F1], $\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-t^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}dt=\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}$. Therefore $\int_{\mathbb R}|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}dt=(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}=1$, since $|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}=(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-t^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}$ by [F4]; consequently $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|\psi|^{2}dx=\left(\int_{\mathbb R}|\psi_{\sigma}|^{2}\right)\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\varphi|^{2}\right)=1$ by Tonelli [F3], so $\psi$ is a unit vector and $[\psi]$ is a pure preparation of the model by [F5]. [given, F1, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 [The position law and its density] By [F2] the law of $Q_{1}$ in the preparation $[\psi]$ is $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{1}^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}dx$; writing the integrand as $|\psi_{\sigma}(x_{1})|^{2}|\varphi(x_{2},x_{3})|^{2}$ by [F4] and iterating the integral by Tonelli [F3], $\int_{x_{1}^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}dx=\left(\int_{B}|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}dt\right)\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\varphi|^{2}\right)=\int_{B}|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}dt$, which is clause (i) with density $f_{1}(t)=|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}$. [given, step 1.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Exact values and bin bounds] By [F2] (the atomless clause of the position law) $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every $\lambda$, so no exact coordinate value carries probability. For the lower bound on a bin with $0\le a<b$, the integrand $|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}$ is decreasing on $[a,b]$, so on $(a,b]$ it is at least $|\psi_{\sigma}(b)|^{2}$; monotonicity of the integral [F3] gives $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}((a,b])\ge\int_{a}^{b}|\psi_{\sigma}(b)|^{2}dt=(b-a)(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-b^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}$, and the symmetric bounds follow for $a=0$, $b=\max\{|a|,|b|\}$ when the bin crosses the origin. The upper bound $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}((a,b])\le(b-a)(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}$ is the same monotonicity with $|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}\le(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}$. For the symmetric bin $(-\sigma,\sigma]$, the substitution $u=t/\sigma$ in step 2.1 gives $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}((-\sigma,\sigma])=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-1}^{1}e^{-u^{2}/2}du$, and since $e^{-1/2}\le e^{-u^{2}/2}\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, monotonicity of the integral [F3] yields $\sqrt{2/(\pi e)}\le\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}((-\sigma,\sigma])\le\sqrt{2/\pi}$; the last displayed bound $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}((-\delta,\delta])\le2\delta/\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}$ is the upper estimate, and positivity of the lower estimate for $\delta=\sigma$ shows that each bin of positive length receives positive probability. [given, step 2.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The transverse factor $\varphi$ enters the computation only through its total mass $\int|\varphi|^{2}=1$; the first-coordinate law of a product state is independent of the transverse profile, while a state that is not a product can correlate the coordinates and change the marginal, as the general density formula $f_{j}(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi(x_{\perp},t)|^{2}dx_{\perp}$ of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-position-and-momentum-outcome-laws]] shows.
- The bounds are deliberately elementary: they neither sharpen the Gaussian integral nor claim an error analysis. They are finite checks of the model's law, not measured frequencies, and no apparatus resolution, binning procedure or count is asserted.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 1.1-1.2 and 2.1.4, printed pages 3-10 and 26-30 (the probability density of the wave function; Gaussian wave packets and their properties)

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 \"Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation\", Section 3, printed pages 11-15 (the position wave function as the component of the state along position states and the normalization of position amplitudes)

items.physical_scope: A finite model computation of position-bin probabilities in the spinless massive-particle model: for a normalized Gaussian packet in the first coordinate and an arbitrary normalized transverse factor, the probability that the first position coordinate lies in a Borel bin is the Gaussian integral over that bin, and the probability of an exact value is zero while every bin of positive length gets positive probability with the stated elementary bounds. The item is conditional on the model's postulates, uses no measured data and asserts no apparatus behaviour.

items.title: The plane wave and the point-localized delta are not preparations of the model
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the massive-particle model postulate P5 of the framework ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]). Then: **every** bounded smooth function $\psi:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C$ that solves the free time-independent Schrödinger equation $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi=E\psi$ pointwise determines a pure preparation of the model with position density $|\psi|^{2}$; in particular the plane wave $\psi_{k}(x)=e^{ik\cdot x}$ with $k\ne0$ is a preparation with constant position density $|\psi_{k}|^{2}=1$, and the point-localized object $\delta^{3}(x-X)$ is the preparation of a particle exactly at $X$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1 and P5 for a spinless particle with state space $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] clauses (i)-(iii), [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] clauses (iii)-(iv)); the position operators $Q_{j}$ with their spectral facts ([[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], [[pthm-nrqm-observables-position-and-momentum-outcome-laws]]); a wave vector $k\in\mathbb R^{3}$, $k\ne0$; a point $X\in\mathbb R^{3}$; the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] **Preparations are rays of the state space.** A pure preparation of the model is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; the zero vector is excluded, and a general preparation is a density operator on $H$. The model assigns no preparation to an object that is not an element of $H$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] clause (ii), [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] **The plane wave has constant modulus and infinite norm.** For every real $\theta$ one has $|e^{i\theta}|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta+\sin^{2}\theta=1$, hence $|e^{ik\cdot x}|^{2}=1$ for every $x$; consequently for the truncations $\mathbf 1_{[-N,N]^{3}}$ one has $\int_{[-N,N]^{3}}|\psi_{k}|^{2}dx=(2N)^{3}$, and monotone convergence gives $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|\psi_{k}|^{2}dx=+\infty$, so $\psi_{k}$ is not an element of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ ([[thm-eulers-formula]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]],).

[F3] **The position observable has no eigenvalues and no atoms.** The spectrum of $Q_{j}$ is all of $\mathbb R$, its outcome law in every preparation is atomless, and by the atom/eigenvalue correspondence it has no eigenvectors: there is no nonzero $x\in H$ with $Q_{j}x=\lambda x$ for any $\lambda$ ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-position-and-momentum-outcome-laws]] clauses (a) and (d), [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F4] **Outcome-law reading.** The model reads an exact position value $\lambda$ through the singleton $\{\lambda\}$ and a finite-resolution outcome through a Borel bin $B$, with probabilities given by the spectral law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; a vector outside $H$ carries no such law.

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct; show that the objects named in the refuted statement are not elements of the state space and that the model's exact-position statement is atomless.

1.1 [The plane wave is not in the state space] By [F2], $|\psi_{k}(x)|^{2}=1$ for every $x$ and $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|\psi_{k}|^{2}dx=+\infty$; hence $\psi_{k}\notin H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$. For every nonzero scalar $z$ the same computation gives $\int|z\psi_{k}|^{2}=|z|^{2}\cdot\infty=\infty$, so no nonzero scalar multiple of $\psi_{k}$ lies in $H$ either, and the formal normalization "$\psi_{k}/\sqrt{V}$" depends on a box volume $V$ and is also not an element of $H$. [given, F2, algebra]

1.2 [The exact-position symbol is not a state] Suppose $x\in H$ were an eigenvector of $Q_{j}$ at some $\lambda$, that is $Q_{j}x=\lambda x$ with $x\ne0$; then $\lambda$ would be an eigenvalue of $Q_{j}$. But [F3] states that $Q_{j}$ has no eigenvalues, and its law is atomless, so no such $x$ exists. The symbol $\delta^{3}(x-X)$ is not a function class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and cannot be an eigenvector; the model's corresponding exact-position statement is instead $\mu^{Q_{j}}(\{X\})=0$ for every preparation. [given, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Hence no preparation is assigned to either object] By [F1] pure preparations are unit rays of $H$ and general preparations are density operators on $H$; since neither $\psi_{k}$ nor $\delta^{3}(x-X)$ determines an element of $H$, neither determines a preparation, and no position density can be attached to them within the model. The identities $|\psi_{k}|^{2}=1$ and "$\delta$ is localized" are formal statements outside the state space, not probabilities of the model. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F4, algebra]

3.1 [The pointwise solution property does not supply a state] Granting that the free plane wave satisfies $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi_{k}=E\psi_{k}$ pointwise with $E=\hbar^{2}|k|^{2}/(2m)$, and that the time-dependent expression $e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}$ with $\omega=E/\hbar$ solves the free Schrödinger equation classically, those are statements about a smooth function on $\mathbb R^{3}$ and do not place it in $H$; the model's dynamics and its Born law are defined on the state space, and by steps 1.1-2.1 the plane wave is not in it. The finite-resolution content of the model is the bin probability of a normalizable packet, not the idealized plane wave: every bin of positive length has positive probability and every exact value has probability zero. This refutes the displayed claim. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, F1, F3, F4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The counterexample concerns the state assignment of this model, not the usefulness of plane waves or delta symbols as distributional tools: they are standard idealizations in formal manipulations, where any probability conclusion requires a separate mathematical statement about normalizable approximants. Nothing here asserts that such approximation schemes fail, only that the raw objects are not preparations and carry no Born law.
- The same argument excludes any bounded solution that does not decay: membership in $H$ is a separate requirement from solving the differential equation, and the model's state postulate assigns states only to elements of $H$.

items.title: A preparation with finite mean position and infinite variance
items.statement:
Work in the spinless massive-particle model of P5 with $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and position operator $Q_{1}$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]], [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]]). Define the symmetric profile
$$g_{0}(t):=\begin{cases}1,&|t|\le1,\\[2pt] |t|^{-3/2},&|t|>1,\end{cases}\qquad Z:=\int_{\mathbb R}|g_{0}(t)|^{2}dt,\qquad g:=Z^{-1/2}g_{0},$$
so that $g\in L^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ has $\|g\|_{2}=1$; fix a unit vector $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{2};\mathbb C)$ and put $\psi(x):=g(x_{1})\varphi(x_{2},x_{3})$. Then $\psi\in H$ is a unit vector, $[\psi]$ is a preparation, and for its position law $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}$ with density $|g|^{2}$:

(i) The mean exists and equals $0$:
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|t|\,|g(t)|^{2}dt<\infty,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}t\,|g(t)|^{2}dt=0,$$
and $\psi\in D(|Q_{1}|^{1/2})$ while $\psi\notin D(Q_{1})$.

(ii) The second moment diverges, so the variance of the position law does not exist:
$$\int_{\mathbb R}t^{2}\,|g(t)|^{2}dt=+\infty,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(t-0\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}(t)=+\infty.$$

Thus a preparation of the model can have a finite mean position without a finite second moment: the moment identities of the framework are conditional on the domains, and a finite mean does not require membership in $D(Q_{1})$.

The example is a model computation; it asserts no measured value and no apparatus behaviour.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The spinless massive model with $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]], [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]]); the profile $g_{0}$, the constant $Z$ and the normalized profile $g=Z^{-1/2}g_{0}$; a unit vector $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{2};\mathbb C)$; the product state $\psi=g\otimes\varphi$; the outcome-law reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] **Power series and harmonic divergence.** $\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-p}$ converges exactly for $p>1$ ([[thm-p-series-real-exponents]]), and a nonnegative series converges if and only if its partial sums are bounded ([[thm-nonnegative-series-bounded-partial-sums]]), so for $p=1$ the partial sums of $\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-1}$ are unbounded and the series diverges to $+\infty$.

[F2] **Block comparison for nonnegative integrals.** On $[k,k+1]$ with $k\ge1$ one has $t^{-2}\le k^{-2}$ and $t^{-1}\ge(k+1)^{-1}$; monotonicity and additivity of the nonnegative Lebesgue integral ([[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]], [[cor-additivity-of-the-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]]) therefore give $\int_{k}^{k+1}t^{-2}dt\le k^{-2}$ and $\int_{k}^{k+1}t^{-1}dt\ge(k+1)^{-1}$ for every $k$, and monotone convergence ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]) passes the resulting bounds to the improper integrals: $\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-2}dt\le\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-2}<\infty$ and $\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-1}dt\ge\sum_{k\ge2}k^{-1}=\infty$.

[F3] **Product states and their position law.** For the unit product state $\psi=g\otimes\varphi$, the law of $Q_{1}$ has density $f_{1}(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi(x_{\perp},t)|^{2}dx_{\perp}=|g(t)|^{2}\int|\varphi|^{2}=|g(t)|^{2}$, and $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every $\lambda$ ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-position-and-momentum-outcome-laws]] clauses (a) and (d), [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]],).

[F4] **Moment criterion.** The mean of the position law is finite exactly when the state lies in $D(|Q_{1}|^{1/2})$, the second moment is finite exactly when it lies in $D(Q_{1})=\{h:x_{1}h\in L^{2}\}$, and for a unit vector in $D(Q_{1})$ the mean is $\langle Q_{1}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and the variance is the second moment minus the square of the mean ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a)-(c), [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F5] **Evenness.** The substitution $t\mapsto-t$ is a $C^{1}$ change of variables with unit Jacobian, so for the even profile $g$ the function $t\mapsto t|g(t)|^{2}$ is odd and its integral over $\mathbb R$ vanishes whenever it is absolutely integrable ([[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; normalize the profile and evaluate the first and second absolute moments by comparison with the $p$-series.

1.1 [The profile is a normalizable $L^{2}$ function] The profile $g_{0}$ is measurable (it is continuous on $|t|>1$ and on $|t|<1$ and bounded near the junction) and nonnegative, and $Z=\int_{-1}^{1}1\,dt+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-3}dt=2+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-3}dt$, where by the block comparison of [F2] with $h(t)=t^{-3}$ the tail satisfies $0<\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-3}dt\le\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-3}<\infty$; hence $0<Z<\infty$ and $g=Z^{-1/2}g_{0}$ is a well-defined element of $L^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ with $\|g\|_{2}^{2}=Z^{-1}Z=1$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [The first moment is finite and the second is infinite] Using evenness and the explicit form of $g$, $\int_{\mathbb R}|t|\,|g(t)|^{2}dt=Z^{-1}\bigl(\int_{-1}^{1}|t|dt+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t\cdot t^{-3}dt\bigr)=Z^{-1}\bigl(1+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-2}dt\bigr)$, which is finite and at least $Z^{-1}>0$ by the bound $\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-2}dt\le\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-2}<\infty$ of [F2]; and $\int_{\mathbb R}t^{2}|g(t)|^{2}dt=Z^{-1}\bigl(\int_{-1}^{1}t^{2}dt+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{2}\cdot t^{-3}dt\bigr)=Z^{-1}\bigl(\tfrac23+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-1}dt\bigr)=+\infty$ because $\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-1}dt\ge\sum_{k\ge2}k^{-1}=\infty$ by [F2] and [F1]. [given, step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [The state and its position law] The product $\psi=g\otimes\varphi$ is an element of $H$ with $\|\psi\|^{2}=\|g\|_{2}^{2}\|\varphi\|^{2}=1$ by Tonelli and the normalizations of step 1.1; hence $[\psi]$ is a pure preparation. By [F3] the law of $Q_{1}$ in this preparation has density $|g|^{2}$ on $\mathbb R$ (independent of $\varphi$), so its first and second absolute moments are exactly the integrals computed in step 2.1, and every exact value has probability zero. [given, step 1.1, F3, algebra]

4.1 [Mean finite, variance infinite] By step 3.1 the position law of the preparation has density $|g|^{2}$, so [F5] applies: the mean $\int t\,d\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}=Z^{-1}\int t|g_{0}(t)|^{2}dt$ vanishes because $t|g_{0}(t)|^{2}$ is odd and integrable by step 2.1, and the mean is finite; the second moment is $+\infty$ by steps 2.1-3.1, so the variance, which is the second moment minus the square of the (zero) mean, does not exist as a finite number. By the criterion [F4] this is exactly the statement $\psi\in D(|Q_{1}|^{1/2})$ but $\psi\notin D(Q_{1})$; the divergence of $\int t^{2}|g|^{2}dt$ is the same as the failure of $x_{1}\psi\in L^{2}$. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F4, F5, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The profile is symmetric, so the finite mean is zero; a non-symmetric variant shifts the mean while keeping the second moment infinite, since the tail exponent $3$ is what decides finiteness: $|g|^{2}$ decays like $t^{-3}$, whose first moment $t\cdot t^{-3}=t^{-2}$ is integrable while the second is not.
- The example shows that the domain hypotheses of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] are not automatic: the state here is a perfectly legitimate preparation of the model, yet the variance of the position law is infinite and the statement "the spread $\Delta Q_{1}$" has no finite value in this preparation.

items.physical_scope: A finite model computation in the spinless massive-particle model exhibiting a legitimate preparation whose position law has a finite mean but infinite second moment: the state is a product of a symmetric profile with a power tail in the first coordinate and an arbitrary normalized transverse factor, its first absolute moment is finite while its second moment diverges, so the mean position exists and the variance of the position law does not. The item asserts no apparatus behaviour, no measured value and no empirical claim; it is a demonstration of the domain hypotheses of the moment statements.

items.title: What the worked readouts of the companion page establish
items.statement:
**Finite energy readout.** [[ex-nrqm-observables-two-level-energy-readout]] computes, on the explicit two-dimensional state space, the spectral measure of the bounded observable $E_{1}P_{1}+E_{2}P_{2}$, the exact outcome probabilities of a pure and of a mixed preparation, and the mean, second moment and variance of the readout. The energies $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$ are parameters of the assigned observable; the computation verifies the framework's law on finite data and asserts no apparatus realization, no measured level and no identification with a specific physical system.

**Position bins.** [[ex-nrqm-observables-position-bin-probabilities]] computes the first-coordinate law of a normalized Gaussian packet in the model's state space, its exact-value probability zero and explicit elementary bounds on the probability of a bin of positive length. The computation verifies the Born density reading of the model on a normalizable state; it reports no counts, no detector response and no resolution, and its bounds are mathematical estimates rather than uncertainty statements about an experiment.

**Distribution caveats.** [[cex-nrqm-observables-plane-wave-is-not-a-preparation]] refutes the informal claim that a free plane wave or a point-localized delta symbol is a preparation of the model: both fail to be elements of the state space, and the model's exact-position statement is that the probability of an exact value is zero. The refutation concerns the state assignment; it does not deny the usefulness of these objects as distributional idealizations, and it makes no claim about approximation schemes in which they are formally employed.

**Domains of the moment statements.** [[ex-nrqm-observables-position-mean-without-variance]] exhibits a legitimate preparation whose position law has a finite mean and infinite second moment, so that the variance of the position law does not exist; the computation verifies that the domain hypotheses of the moment statements are genuine and not automatic. It asserts no measurement error, no disturbance and no apparatus behaviour.

**Empirical neutrality.** None of the four items is an experiment. Each is a finite or asymptotic computation inside the model's state space and outcome law, or a refutation of an informal claim about that model; none records data, calibration, sampling, uncertainty or a comparison with observation. Agreement or disagreement with data would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions and is not established or claimed here.
